claims.statement: Directive 2023/970 requires employers with 150-249 workers to provide the specified prior-year pay information by 7 June 2027 and every three years thereafter; employers with 100-149 workers start by 7 June 2031.

The Commission says employers must provide pay-range information to applicants, give workers specified pay information, report gender pay gaps from 100 employees, and conduct a pay assessment when an unexplained gap reaches at least 5% under the rule's conditions.

Poland's Labour Inspectorate described implementation as a significant practical challenge and anticipated increased complaints and demand for employer guidance, but national details remain material to delivery.

contrary_evidence: Formal reporting for 150-249 employee firms is only every three years, and the 100-149 band does not start until 2031.
Large payroll suites and compensation consultancies can add similar analytics to existing contracts.
National transposition may supply public analytical methods or materially alter timing and process.

economics.acquisition_route: Revenue share with payroll bureaus and employment-law firms serving the 150-249 employee band
economics.founder_net_worth_path: Scenario, not evidence: 600 employers averaging PLN 24,000 annual revenue yields PLN 14.4m revenue; at a 45% operating margin, several mature years of dividends and retained cash could produce PLN 20m-plus founder net worth
economics.founder_time: Three to four hours per day with a fixed file intake window and partner-owned legal or employee-relations meetings
economics.gross_margin_basis: Data ingestion and repeat analysis can exceed 80% gross margin; job-architecture review and legal-partner share reduce first-cycle blended margin
economics.payback: Target immediate payback because the first diagnostic is paid in stages before analysis and review
economics.pricing: Assumption: PLN 12,000-40,000 for the first diagnostic and methodology cycle plus PLN 6,000-18,000 per year for monitoring and report refresh
economics.retention_or_repeat: Annual hiring, raises, reorganisations, and employee information requests create monitoring demand even though formal reporting for this band is every three years

fingerprint.compounding_advantage: A non-personal multilingual job-architecture library and correction corpus that improves title normalisation and explainable comparator suggestions without pooling customer pay data
fingerprint.customer: EU employers with 150-249 workers and fragmented payroll or job architecture, initially Polish industrial, services, and technology firms without an internal compensation-analytics team
fingerprint.distribution_mechanism: Payroll bureaus and employment-law firms bundle the workbench into existing annual services and retain legal interpretation while the product handles analysis
fingerprint.offer_and_business_model: Privacy-preserving analytics workspace for job-value taxonomy, gap decomposition, explainable comparators, remediation scenarios, methodology records, and report exports; first-cycle project plus annual subscription
fingerprint.payer_and_paid_event: The CFO or HR director pays when a pseudonymised payroll file is converted into reviewed job categories and a pre-report diagnostic, then pays annually for monitoring and scenario updates
fingerprint.problem_trigger: EU pay-transparency rules require this size band to report specified gender-pay information by 7 June 2027 and every three years thereafter, while an unjustified gap of at least 5% can trigger a joint pay assessment

founder_fit: Statistical decomposition, bias diagnostics, and explainable clustering strongly match data-science skills
The finance interest aligns with CFO-facing compensation modelling
Payroll and legal partners can handle meetings and jurisdiction-specific advice
A pseudonymised file-based pilot is bounded, measurable, and compatible with continued employment
risks: A biased or opaque classification can amplify discrimination rather than diagnose it.
Employee compensation data creates severe privacy and access-control obligations.
Incorrect outputs could lead to disputes, claims, or damaging remediation decisions.
Partner-led legal review may compress margin and create delivery bottlenecks.

structure.commercial_archetype: Periodic analytical compliance workbench with annual monitoring subscription
structure.control_point: The documented job-category and equal-value methodology that determines every downstream gap calculation and remediation scenario
structure.critical_dependency: A lawful, explainable methodology accepted by management and worker representatives under each country's transposition

thesis: An explainable pay-equity workbench can help 150-249-employee EU firms turn inconsistent titles and payroll exports into gender-neutral job categories, gap decompositions, scenario tests, and an audit-ready methodology before their first 7 June 2027 report. The Poland beachhead should be sold through payroll and employment-law partners because national transposition details may vary and employee-level outputs demand legal and worker-representative review.
title: Pay-Equity Model Room for 150-249-Employee Firms
uncertainties: Poland's final transposition details and authority-provided methodology must be verified before a domestic product promise.
Employers may purchase a one-time consultant project rather than retain annual software.
The quality of job-title and payroll data, worker-representative involvement, and review labour are unmeasured.
Pricing and the 600-employer wealth scenario have no demand validation.
